newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher then retreat.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher then retreat.

text.p: French shares pushed higher at the open on Monday, drawing comfort from a strong dollar versus the mark and shrugging off Wall Street's lower close on Friday.
Traders said the steady dollar gave market support.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 9.68 points or 0.37 percent at 2,617.23 at 0933 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up one at 2,525 from Friday's close.
"The market remains solid despite the retreat on Wall Street," said one market professional.
Volume was 458 million francs within the first half hour.

Renault sheds 4.4 percent to 140.5. Brokerage Oddo upgraded the stock to overweight from sell, following the planned closure of the Vilvoorde Belgian car factory and reports of 3,100 French jobs to go. It revised down its earnings estimates to a loss of 20.1 francs for 1996 versus loss 3.1, a 1997 loss of 2.1 francs versus loss 0.6, and 1998 profit 2.1 versus 3.3.
Another French broker said, "We like it (the stock)," adding that the restructuring was needed to cut capacity.
SEB dropped heavily, falling 5.4 percent to 1,012 francs, after the electrical appliances firm reported a seven percent increase in 1996 profit.
Elf Gabon suspended after rising 20 percent on news it is paying a special dividend of $75 per share with the planned liquidation of CPIH in which it holds 65 percent.
Credit Lyonnais continues speculative rise, up 2.87 percent at 233.
The head of rival commercial bank Societe Generale, Marc Vienot, reiterated a call for the breakup and liquidation of Credit Lyonnais, which needs another state bailout.
